items.note: Introduces the Semantic Repulsion Technique for AI writing help and compares it with baseline systems computationally and in a 16-person user study rated on usefulness, coherence, and originality; unclear whether participants wrote with each system or only rated its outputs, and N is far below 50.
Compares Alternate Uses Task responses of 256 humans with those of three AI chatbots; no participant uses AI; an Author Correction exists (10.1038/s41598-024-54745-y).

Controlled experiment with 148 participants brainstorming with an AI partner that either deepens or diversifies ideas (one AI configuration versus another); outcomes named are trust and idea adoption, so a creativity score on the output may not exist.

Three groups of professional engineers and designers produce speculative-design ideas without AI, with AI as a tool, or fully by AI; experts rate 120 ideas on novelty, usefulness, and craft, and cosine similarity measures design-space spread; group assignment and N not stated, and the sample is likely small.

Within-group experiment in which 35 UX design students generate 214 concepts with and without ChatGPT, with expert creativity ratings plus self-reports; order randomization not stated and N is below 50.

385 participants complete five rounds of story writing in an AI creativity-training program under four conditions (automated feedback or not, adaptive or constant difficulty), with pre/post Alternate Uses Task scores; check whether the feedback is generative AI and whether any arm lacks AI (all arms use the program).

Two preregistered parallel experiments (1,100 participants in total, per-experiment N not given) compare a standard LLM, a coach-like LLM, and no AI on divergent and convergent thinking, including a final unassisted stage (after_ai); the title states randomization; same study as arXiv 2410.03703.

Observational analysis of 2.1 million preprints, 28,000 review reports, and 246 million accesses; LLM adopters produce more papers and cite more diverse prior work, but no novelty or similarity measure of the papers themselves is named, so it may belong in out (no_creativity_or_diversity_outcome); abstract from arXiv 2601.13187 (author version), OpenAlex holds only the editorial summary.

Longitudinal analysis of 81,663 college admissions essays (2020 to 2024) at one selective university, with detector-estimated LLM use; reports post-2023 convergence in surface linguistic features by socioeconomic status.

Difference-in-differences around ChatGPT's release on an open innovation platform; outcomes are participation, work length, complexity, and votes, with no diversity or novelty measure, so it may belong in out (no_creativity_or_diversity_outcome); abstract from the Springer landing page.
